headline: Black Robin Bounces Back From Brink of Extinction
meta_description: New Zealand's black robin has recovered from a single breeding pair to 350 adults through a pioneering conservation programme.
summary_short: Once facing extinction with just one breeding pair, New Zealand's black robin now thrives with 350 adults—and wins bird of the year.
body:
New Zealand's black robin has soared from the edge of extinction to a population of 350 adults, earning the nation's bird of the year title. The recovery marks a remarkable turnaround for a species that once existed as a single breeding pair.

A pioneering breeding programme made the rescue possible, transforming the black robin's prospects through dedicated conservation efforts. The species' journey from near-total loss to sustainable population growth demonstrates how focused scientific work can pull a bird back from the brink.

The award recognises not just the species itself, but the underlying commitment to restoration that gave the black robin a second chance at survival in New Zealand.
quick_facts: Black robin population grew to 350 adults
Once existed as only one breeding pair
Recovery achieved through pioneering breeding programme
Won New Zealand bird of the year award
